Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; built on 3.2.0 PTR values Blizzard may revise. This is rogue-meta-penetrating-shot with the Trap package taken seriously instead of taken incidentally. The meta build carries Smoke Grenade mainly to bank Tricks of the Trade's Trap category; this variant builds around it, because 3.2.0 buffed the entire grenade line at once: Grenadier's Aspect went 35-50%[x] to 45-60%[x] and, crucially, 52.5-75%[x] to 75-100%[x] against Crowd Controlled enemies, while Smoke Grenade's Shade Grenade variant gained Combo Point damage and Shade damage bonuses. Since Smoke Grenade also applies the crowd control that unlocks Grenadier's higher band, the build supplies its own condition - and Applied Alchemy's 5-piece went 200%[x] to 250%[x] on top. The trade is real: less raw single-target than the meta build, more consistent pack damage and better survivability from Aspect of Poisonous Clouds' new 7-10%[x] damage reduction on Poisoned enemies.

Rotation
  1. Smoke Grenade, then Penetrating Shot, on repeat.
  2. Lead every pack with Shadow Clone, keep Poison Imbuement up by attacking, and fight at grenade range rather than bow range.
Variants

Leveling — Smoke Grenade into the pack to crowd-control it, then Penetrating Shot through the line while Grenadier's higher band is active. Poison Imbuement maintained by attacking, Dash between packs, Shadow Clone on elites.
Move on when Level 70 with Torment 1 unlocked and Aspect of Imitated Imbuement in hand - the same gate as the base build.

Early Endgame — Smoke Grenade first, always. It crowd-controls the pack, which flips Grenadier's Aspect from 45-60%[x] to 75-100%[x], and only then is Penetrating Shot worth firing. Shadow Clone for the Vulnerable window, Poison Imbuement maintained by attacking, Dash to reposition. The mental model is grenade-then-shot, not shot-with-occasional-grenade.
Move on when The Sightless Set assembled and Grenadier's Aspect at a usable roll. Both matter - without Grenadier's this is just the base build with a worse talisman.

Late Endgame — Grenade, then shot, on repeat. With the Sightless Set online Shadow Clone comes back almost immediately, so lead packs with it. Aspect of Poisonous Clouds' new rider means every Poisoned enemy is also dealing 7-10%[x] less damage to you, which is what lets this variant fight at grenade range instead of at bow range.
Move on when Comfortable clears of pack-dense content - Challenge Dungeons and Overland Ambushes are the 3.2.0 activities this variant is tuned for. If your content is boss-heavy, swap to rogue-meta-penetrating-shot instead of pushing this.

Pushing — Push with the honest limitation stated: Grenadier's 75-100%[x] band requires crowd-controlled targets, and Pit bosses resist crowd control, so this variant's ceiling on a boss fight is the lower 45-60%[x] band plus whatever the base build already had. Against dense corridors it is the better build; against a boss room it is not, and the correct move is to swap rather than to force it. All values are 3.2.0 PTR values and may change before Season 15 launches.

Uniques
  • weapon PTR route: PTR Boosts from the vendor Mrak next to the main Waypoint in any major city. Live route (Season 14, unchanged by 3.2.0): target-farm Echo of Varshan at Initiate lair tier (1 Lair Key, Torment 1+), then upgrade via the Horadric Cube - on 3.2.0 the 'Upgrade Direct Item to Mythic' recipe transfers your rolled affixes 1:1, so roll the bow first and convert second. Where →
  • offhand PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: target-farm Harbinger of Hatred at Greater Lair tier (1 Greater Lair Key). Where →
  • helm Mythic Unique, all classes. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: craft at the Jeweler from Resplendent Sparks and Runes choosing the helm slot - no Crafted tag on 3.2.0, so it does not consume your one crafted-Mythic slot; or a Blacksmith Mythic cache; or any boss drop. Where →
  • gloves PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: no dedicated boss - farm via the Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe (Common gloves plus 1 Enhanced Primordial Dust and 10 Primordial Dust). Note the tension: Grenadier's Aspect wants a gloves slot too, so on this variant Fists of Fate competes with the aspect rather than complementing it - run Grenadier's on gloves and Fists of Fate only if you can place the aspect elsewhere. Where →
  • chest PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: target-farm Harbinger of Hatred at Greater Lair tier (1 Greater Lair Key). Where →
  • amulet PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0; exists in Season 14's general unique pool. Doubled to 15-20%[x] on the PTR and category-neutral, so it pays on grenades and arrows alike. Where →
  • SSplinter of Anguish jewelry socket New Soul Splinter socketable, jewelry only. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts include Soul Splinters. Live route: unpublished. Anguish, not Hellfire - Hellfire's -100% Critical Strike Chance is disqualifying for a crit-scaling build. Its +30% Primary Resource cost is easier to carry here than on the base build because grenade damage is gated by cooldowns rather than Energy. Where →
  • Target-farm The Butcher, a Greater-tier Lair boss (1x Greater Lair Key) - the dedicated source for this item. Where →

No 3.2.0 skill tree is published for any build on any site - the official notes carry no allocations, and Maxroll, Icy Veins, d4builds and d4guides were all still serving Season 14 guides on 2026-08-08, day 5 of the 8-day PTR. This allocation is therefore the specialist's, built from the skill list the PTR digest authorises for this class plus the 3.2.0 changes that actually apply. Treat the point counts as a starting shape to test, not as a published build. Where a skill's upgrade mods are named below, those names are carried over from Season 14 planner data - 3.2.0 does not rename them. Where a skill appears with no mods, that is deliberate: its mod names were not published anywhere consulted, and inventing them would be worse than leaving them out. On the PTR you can skip this stage - Mrak's boosts grant level 70 and maxed aspects directly - so it is written for a live Season 15. Specialization while levelling is Combo Points; note that there is no Death Trap specialization in this version of the game, only Inner Sight, Preparation and Combo Points.

Skill point priority

  2. Forceful Arrow for Energy
  3. Smoke Grenade earlier than the base build takes it, so you learn its radius and timing before it becomes load-bearing
  4. Poison Imbuement for the attacking-maintains-uptime loop
  5. Dash for mobility. Its Shadow Play variant is renamed Echo on the PTR - same skill
  6. Shadow Clone as the ultimate

Skills to select4 picks

  • Incendiary BoltPassive
  • Scorched EarthPassive

    Roughly 30% more damage-over-time taken from you - the reason Subo is hired over Raheir here.

  • SnipeIconic skill

How to run them

[ptr] 3.2.0 changes nothing about mercenaries - no mercenary name appears anywhere in the official 3.2.0 notes. This is the Season 14 Poison Penetrating Shot pairing carried over, which is the only guidance that exists. Hire Subo and take Incendiary Bolt, Scorched Earth, Snipe and Molotov; Scorched Earth's roughly 30% increase to your damage-over-time is what makes him the Poison variant's pick over Raheir, who the Cold variant hires instead. Reinforce with Varyana on Bloodthirst, Opportunity trigger Penetrating Shot. Icy Veins reinforces with Raheir/Bastion off Dark Shroud instead; that disagreement predates the PTR and 3.2.0 does nothing to settle it. One variant-specific note: Subo is a trap-and-marking mercenary and this is the trap-weighted variant, so the hire fits here even better than it does on the base build.

Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; built on 3.2.0 PTR values Blizzard may revise. This is rogue-meta-penetrating-shot with the Trap package taken seriously instead of taken incidentally. The meta build carries Smoke Grenade mainly to bank Tricks of the Trade's Trap category; this variant builds around it, because 3.2.0 buffed the entire grenade line at once: Grenadier's Aspect went 35-50%[x] to 45-60%[x] and, crucially, 52.5-75%[x] to 75-100%[x] against Crowd Controlled enemies, while Smoke Grenade's Shade Grenade variant gained Combo Point damage and Shade damage bonuses. Since Smoke Grenade also applies the crowd control that unlocks Grenadier's higher band, the build supplies its own condition - and Applied Alchemy's 5-piece went 200%[x] to 250%[x] on top. The trade is real: less raw single-target than the meta build, more consistent pack damage and better survivability from Aspect of Poisonous Clouds' new 7-10%[x] damage reduction on Poisoned enemies.

Rotation
  1. Smoke Grenade, then Penetrating Shot, on repeat.
  2. Lead every pack with Shadow Clone, keep Poison Imbuement up by attacking, and fight at grenade range rather than bow range.
Variants

Leveling — Smoke Grenade into the pack to crowd-control it, then Penetrating Shot through the line while Grenadier's higher band is active. Poison Imbuement maintained by attacking, Dash between packs, Shadow Clone on elites.
Move on when Level 70 with Torment 1 unlocked and Aspect of Imitated Imbuement in hand - the same gate as the base build.

Early Endgame — Smoke Grenade first, always. It crowd-controls the pack, which flips Grenadier's Aspect from 45-60%[x] to 75-100%[x], and only then is Penetrating Shot worth firing. Shadow Clone for the Vulnerable window, Poison Imbuement maintained by attacking, Dash to reposition. The mental model is grenade-then-shot, not shot-with-occasional-grenade.
Move on when The Sightless Set assembled and Grenadier's Aspect at a usable roll. Both matter - without Grenadier's this is just the base build with a worse talisman.

Late Endgame — Grenade, then shot, on repeat. With the Sightless Set online Shadow Clone comes back almost immediately, so lead packs with it. Aspect of Poisonous Clouds' new rider means every Poisoned enemy is also dealing 7-10%[x] less damage to you, which is what lets this variant fight at grenade range instead of at bow range.
Move on when Comfortable clears of pack-dense content - Challenge Dungeons and Overland Ambushes are the 3.2.0 activities this variant is tuned for. If your content is boss-heavy, swap to rogue-meta-penetrating-shot instead of pushing this.

Pushing — Push with the honest limitation stated: Grenadier's 75-100%[x] band requires crowd-controlled targets, and Pit bosses resist crowd control, so this variant's ceiling on a boss fight is the lower 45-60%[x] band plus whatever the base build already had. Against dense corridors it is the better build; against a boss room it is not, and the correct move is to swap rather than to force it. All values are 3.2.0 PTR values and may change before Season 15 launches.

  • weapon PTR route: PTR Boosts from the vendor Mrak next to the main Waypoint in any major city. Where →
  • offhand PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: target-farm Harbinger of Hatred at Greater Lair tier (1 Greater Lair Key). Where →
  • helm Mythic Unique, all classes. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: craft at the Jeweler from Resplendent Sparks and Runes choosing the helm slot - no Crafted tag on 3.2.0, so it does not consume your one crafted-Mythic slot; or a Blacksmith Mythic cache; or any boss drop. Where →
  • gloves PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: no dedicated boss - farm via the Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe (Common gloves plus 1 Enhanced Primordial Dust and 10 Primordial Dust). Note the tension: Grenadier's Aspect wants a gloves slot too, so on this variant Fists of Fate competes with the aspect rather than complementing it - run Grenadier's on gloves and Fists of Fate only if you can place the aspect elsewhere. Where →
  • chest PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: target-farm Harbinger of Hatred at Greater Lair tier (1 Greater Lair Key). Where →
  • amulet PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0; exists in Season 14's general unique pool. Doubled to 15-20%[x] on the PTR and category-neutral, so it pays on grenades and arrows alike. Where →
  • SSplinter of Anguish jewelry socket New Soul Splinter socketable, jewelry only. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts include Soul Splinters. Live route: unpublished. Anguish, not Hellfire - Hellfire's -100% Critical Strike Chance is disqualifying for a crit-scaling build. Its +30% Primary Resource cost is easier to carry here than on the base build because grenade damage is gated by cooldowns rather than Energy. Where →
  • Target-farm The Butcher, a Greater-tier Lair boss (1x Greater Lair Key) - the dedicated source for this item. Where →

Reasoning

Based onPoison Penetrating Shot Rogue
Tweaks vs. the base build
  1. Grenadier's Aspect promoted from unused to core, on gloves. On the PTR it reaches 75-100%[x] against Crowd Controlled enemies, and Smoke Grenade is the crowd control - the build creates its own trigger condition rather than hoping for one.
  2. Smoke Grenade is played on cooldown as a damage skill rather than pressed occasionally for utility. Its Shade Grenade variant now gains Combo Point damage and Shade damage bonuses when using Combo Points, which is a change the meta build does not exploit.
  3. Talisman swap: Nilfur's Narrow Eye out, Applied Alchemy 5-piece in. Narrow Eye's PTR gain is extended Marksman range, which suits the meta build's line-up-the-shot game; Applied Alchemy's 200%[x] to 250%[x] is category-neutral and pays on the grenade damage too.
  4. Aspect swap: Aspect of Alchemical Advantage out, Grenadier's Aspect in on gloves. Alchemical Advantage scales with Poison stacking on a single target; Grenadier's pays on every grenade against every crowd-controlled enemy, which is the shape of this variant's damage.
  5. Aspect of Poisonous Clouds is mandatory here rather than optional. Its new PTR rider makes Poisoned enemies deal 7-10%[x] reduced damage, and this variant spends more time at mid range inside the grenade radius than the meta build does at long range.
  6. Paragon reweighting: Tricks of the Trade is still first, but weight the Trap side of the tree over the Marksman side. The meta build takes the reverse weighting.
  7. Soul Splinter unchanged: Splinter of Anguish, never Splinter of Hellfire - the -100% Critical Strike Chance disqualifies Hellfire for any crit-scaling Rogue. Anguish's +30% Primary Resource cost is more affordable here than on the meta build because grenades cost cooldowns rather than Energy.
  8. Do not take this variant for boss-only content. Grenadier's higher band needs crowd-controlled targets and bosses resist crowd control - against a single boss the meta build is straightforwardly better and you should swap.

AgilityCutthroatImbueableMobility

Charge Cooldown: 12 seconds

SubterfugeGrenade

Rank 15/15

Cooldown: 10 seconds

Lucky Hit Chance: 25%

Throw a smoky concoction at enemies that deals 90% damage and Dazes them for 4 seconds.

Modifiers

  • SilhouetteSmoke Grenade no longer Dazes enemies and instead creates a cloud of shadows at your feet. While within the cloud, you gain +5.0% Critical Strike Chance and Stealth once every 1 second.

Poison Imbuement

Imbuements

Rank 15/15

Cooldown: 20 seconds

Lucky Hit Chance: 33%

Imbue your weapons with lethal poison for 6 seconds. While imbued, your Imbueable Skills deal Poison damage and apply 100% of their Base damage as additional Poisoning damage over 6 seconds.

Modifiers

  • PToxic TouchPoison Imbuement gains 40%[x] increased Potency. Each successive time an enemy is Poisoned by Poison Imbuement, the Potency of Poison Imbuement against the enemy is increased by 5%[x], up to 50%[x].
  • DurationPoison Imbuement's duration is increased by 2 seconds. Casting Poison Imbuement consumes up to 2 stacks of Ferocity to further increase its duration by 2 per Ferocity spent.
  • CooldownLucky Hit: Poison Imbued Skills have up to a 30% chance to reduce the Cooldown of Poison Imbuement by 2 seconds.
Poison Damage

Shadow Clone

UltimateCutthroat

Rank 1/15

Cooldown: 60 seconds

Summon a shadow that mimics your actions for 15 seconds. This Shadow Clone deals 40% of your damage.

Modifiers

  • SentryShadow Clone becomes a Marksman Skill and now summons a stationary shadow that fires 3 piercing arrows every 1.0 seconds. Each arrow deals 20% damage. Shadow Clone gains 2 additional Charges, and its Cooldown is reduced by 20 seconds. You may have up to 3 Shadow Clones active at a time.
  • CooldownShadow Clone's Cooldown is reduced by 10 seconds.
  • Weaken & VulnerableCasting Shadow Clone makes all Nearby enemies Weakened and Vulnerable for 6 seconds.

Surround yourself with up to 5 protective shadows. Gain +8.0% Resistance to All Elements per active shadow. If you have the maximum amount of shadows, direct damage is reduced by 20.0%. Each time you take direct damage, a shadow is consumed.

Modifiers

  • OverflowDark Shroud no longer grants Resistance to All Elements, but instead grants you 15% increased Energy Regeneration per shadow.
  • Consume ChanceDark Shroud shadows have a 15% chance to not be consumed.
  • Movement SpeedEach active Dark Shroud shadow grants you 5%[x] Movement Speed.

Shadow Clone

UltimateCutthroat

Rank 1/15

Cooldown: 60 seconds

Summon a shadow that mimics your actions for 15 seconds. This Shadow Clone deals 40% of your damage.

Modifiers

  • SentryShadow Clone becomes a Marksman Skill and now summons a stationary shadow that fires 3 piercing arrows every 1.0 seconds. Each arrow deals 20% damage. Shadow Clone gains 2 additional Charges, and its Cooldown is reduced by 20 seconds. You may have up to 3 Shadow Clones active at a time.
  • CooldownShadow Clone's Cooldown is reduced by 10 seconds.
  • Weaken & VulnerableCasting Shadow Clone makes all Nearby enemies Weakened and Vulnerable for 6 seconds.
